chapter: Moten band, arranging and the guitar
title: Makers of amplified and resonator guitars
summary: He names Ampliphone, Gibson, Stella and National resonators and describes the odd sound he got on Battles' records.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Who were the first people to make a proper amplified guitar?
Yeah, that's what I was using. Ampliphone and Gibson.
Yeah. Who were the big guitar people in those -- before that came in?
Well, the accoustic guitar was a -- the Stella guitar was one I used on lots of records. Honey, Keep Your Mind on Me, and then I came in with a --
What was National? Wasn't that a --
That metal guitar, yeah. That's the one that made that.
I was thinking about, maybe I would get me a resonator guitar and rig it up, because I remember the first --

Well, what were some of those records that you made with -- (unintelligible) Battles records. You get a sort of -- I don't know what sort of guitar you were using, but you get a sort of jungly sort of sound on it.
Yes, in between electric piano, ain't it?
It was a strange -- it was a very effective sound, though. I wondered whether you were --
I was using a Dan electric, and it had a peculiar sound to a certain extent. But I could and take anybody else's guitar and get that sound. It's the way you grip in here.
